data.name: Jaishree
data.gender_notes: Jaishree is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jaishree is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Jai’ meaning victory and ‘Shree’ meaning God. This name signifies the victory of God in one's life. It is a name often given to a girl born in Hindu families, signifying the victory of the divine over the mundane. The name Jaishree carries the meaning “Victory of God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jaishree usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

vedic_reference.note: The name Jaishree is derived from the Sanskrit words jaya, meaning victory, and shree, meaning prosperity. It is a popular name among Hindus and is believed to bring good fortune and success.

historical_references.reference: Jaishree was a queen consort of the Chalukya emperor, Vijayaditya Satakarni (reigned c. 733-746 CE). She is known for her military campaigns, particularly her successful defense of Badami against the invading Pallava forces.

Jaishree is also mentioned in several medieval Hindu texts as a princess and a devotee of the god Shiva. She is particularly known for her association with the temple of Kedarnath in the Himalayas, where she is said to have performed penance and received divine blessings.
